correctness.rationale: Using cyclic vertex separation k (1<=k<=floor(n/2)), the exact minimax center distance equals chord length d_{ceil(k/2)} because cyclic index triangle inequality gives the lower bound and the shorter-arc midpoint vertex attains it. Thus leipodistance g_k=4R*sin(ceil(k/2)*pi/n)-2R*sin(k*pi/n). Every even k is dominated by preceding odd k, and for odd k=2m+1 the derivative of F(u)=4R*sin(u)-2R*sin(2u-pi/n) is 4R*(cos(u)-cos(2u-pi/n))>=0 throughout the admissible interval. The largest allowed odd k maximizes; substitution gives all four residue-class formulas and Taylor expansions, with limiting circle gap 2(sqrt(2)-1)R. Independently enumerated all vertex-pair/vertex-center minimaxes for n=3..50 and matched the exact formula numerically; the proof is all-n and finite enumeration was only a check.
residual_risks: Ambient chord metric with centers constrained to vertex set; not polygon boundary/intrinsic metric, irregular samples or higher-dimensional spheres.
